run.question:
You are an SRE agent tasked with diagnosing issues in a Kubernetes application.

Application: OpenTelemetry Demo Astronomy Shop
Namespace: astronomy-shop

An online shopping platform built with a microservices architecture, showcasing OpenTelemetry instrumentation for distributed tracing across services.

CRITICAL: You are running in an AUTOMATED environment. Work autonomously and make all decisions yourself. DO NOT ask for user confirmation or approval. Proceed with the best solution based on your analysis.

TASK: DIAGNOSIS
- Investigate the application to detect any anomalies or issues
- Analyze metrics, logs, and traces
- When ready, submit a natural language description of the issue you found
- Your diagnosis is evaluated on whether you correctly identify the faulty components and root cause

Important:
- You can query metrics and traces through the available observability tools

report.summary: The checkout service is down because its Deployment pod template carries a nodeSelector that no node in the cluster satisfies. Deployment checkout in namespace astronomy-shop has spec.template.spec.nodeSelector {"kubernetes.io/hostname": "extra-node"}; the only nodes are sregym-control-plane, sregym-worker, sregym-worker2 and sregym-worker3, so every checkout pod is Unschedulable and checkout has 0 ready/available replicas and a Service with no endpoints. At 03:31:53 checkout is the only one of 24 deployments in the namespace with 0 ready replicas; all others read 1. The rollout that introduced this state is visible in events: the previously working pod checkout-6c769b88b5-ntls4 started at 03:31:16, was stopped at 03:31:36, and ReplicaSets checkout-54579c864c (03:31:36) and checkout-c69887c97 (03:31:42) were created carrying the bad nodeSelector, with both of their pods failing to schedule. On the caller side, frontend logged gRPC '14 UNAVAILABLE ... connect: ECONNREFUSED 10.96.183.199:8080' (the checkout ClusterIP) and, at 03:31:53, error span counts existed only for the frontend checkout path (frontend oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder 1, POST /api/checkout 2, tcp.connect 2), frontend-proxy (2+2) and load-generator (POST 1); no other service had STATUS_CODE_ERROR spans. Checkout itself was serving successfully (PlaceOrder rpc.grpc.status_code=0) at ~03:31:30 before the rollout, and the flagd demo flags are all defaultVariant "off", so a flagd fault and a cluster-wide node problem were considered and rejected as this cause. Limit: Kubernetes objects are point-in-time, Prometheus range queries returned no data in this run, and Jaeger/pod-log data stops around 03:31:32-03:31:53, so failures after the 03:31:36 rollout are inferred from 0 available replicas and an empty endpoints object rather than observed request errors.

claims.text: Deployment checkout in namespace astronomy-shop has spec.template.spec.nodeSelector {"kubernetes.io/hostname": "extra-node"} and status conditions Available=False (MinimumReplicasUnavailable) / Progressing=True (ReplicaSetUpdated), with replicas 2 and unavailableReplicas 2.

The cluster has exactly four nodes with kubernetes.io/hostname labels sregym-control-plane, sregym-worker, sregym-worker2 and sregym-worker3; only the control plane carries the node-role.kubernetes.io/control-plane taint and all four report Ready=True. No node has the hostname extra-node.

Both checkout pods are Pending with no container statuses, owned by ReplicaSets checkout-54579c864c and checkout-c69887c97, and their PodScheduled condition is False with reason Unschedulable and message '0/4 nodes are available: 1 node(s) had untolerated taint {node-role.kubernetes.io/control-plane: }, 3 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector'.

Events of 2026-11-24T03:31:36Z and 03:31:42Z record FailedScheduling for checkout-54579c864c-xnts7 and checkout-c69887c97-qkbmk with that same 0/4 nodes message, and the pod list shows exactly these two pods as Pending while all other 26 pods in the namespace are Running and ready.

Both checkout ReplicaSets carry the same bad selector: checkout-54579c864c (created 2026-11-24T03:31:36Z, revision 1) and checkout-c69887c97 (created 2026-11-24T03:31:42Z, revision 2) both have spec.template.spec.nodeSelector {"kubernetes.io/hostname": "extra-node"}.

Events show the mechanism as a rollout of checkout: checkout-6c769b88b5-ntls4 was scheduled and its checkout container started at 03:31:16Z, 'Stopping container checkout' was recorded at 03:31:36Z, and the same minute the Deployment scaled up ReplicaSet checkout-54579c864c, followed by checkout-c69887c97 at 03:31:42Z.

checkout is the only deployment in astronomy-shop with 0 ready and 0 available replicas: kube_deployment_status_replicas_available{deployment="checkout"} = 0 and kube_deployment_status_replicas_ready{deployment="checkout"} = 0 at 2026-11-24T03:31:53Z, while the other 23 deployments each read 1, and every other deployment has nodeSelector null.
kube_pod_status_unschedulable = 1 for pod checkout-54579c864c-xnts7 at 2026-11-24T03:31:53Z, and kube_pod_status_phase shows that pod Pending=1 (Running=0, Failed=0) at the same instant.
Service checkout has clusterIP 10.96.183.199 and its endpoints object has subsets null, i.e. the service has no backing addresses.

frontend pod frontend-6859c775df-qtbx6 logged 'Error: 14 UNAVAILABLE: No connection established. Last error: connect ECONNREFUSED 10.96.183.199:8080' at 2026-11-24T03:31:04Z and again at 03:31:12Z, where 10.96.183.199 is the checkout ClusterIP.

At 2026-11-24T03:31:53Z the only error span series are in the checkout call path: frontend oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder=1, frontend executing api route (pages) /api/checkout=1, frontend POST /api/checkout=2, frontend tcp.connect=2, frontend-proxy router frontend egress=2, frontend-proxy POST=2 and load-generator POST=1; no checkout, cart, payment, product-catalog or other service series carry STATUS_CODE_ERROR.

Before the rollout checkout was serving normally: traces at ~03:31:30Z contain complete PlaceOrder traces with checkout server span oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder rpc.grpc.status_code=0, frontend POST /api/checkout http.status_code=200 and load-generator POST http.status_code=200.

The nodeSelector {"kubernetes.io/hostname": "extra-node"} added to the checkout Deployment pod template at ~03:31:36Z (managedFieldsSummary: kubectl-client-side-apply Update 03:31:36Z, OpenAPI-Generator Update 03:31:42Z) is the fault: it is the only setting in the workload that makes both checkout pods unschedulable and drives the deployment to zero available replicas and an endpoint-less Service.

Fault injection through flagd is not this cause: every flag in ConfigMap flagd-config (including cartFailure, paymentFailure, paymentUnreachable, productCatalogFailure, adFailure, checkout-relevant load flags) is ENABLED but has defaultVariant "off", and no service other than frontend/frontend-proxy/load-generator shows error spans.

A node-level shortage or node loss is not this cause: all four nodes are Ready=True with no non-control-plane taints, and the FailedScheduling message rules out resource exhaustion, naming an untolerated control-plane taint on one node plus a Pod node affinity/selector mismatch on the other three.

Checked and healthy: all other 23 deployments in astronomy-shop (accounting, ad, cart, currency, email, flagd, fraud-detection, frontend, frontend-proxy, grafana, image-provider, jaeger, kafka, llm, load-generator, payment, postgresql, product-catalog, product-reviews, quote, recommendation, shipping, valkey-cart) report 1 ready and 1 available replica at 03:31:53Z, and their pods are Running with 0 restarts; startup-only noise (grafana configmap FailedMount, opensearch/otel-collector startup probe misses, opensearch-pdb NoPods at 03:30:52Z, otel-collector-agent DaemonSet roll) had cleared by then.

Remove the nodeSelector {"kubernetes.io/hostname": "extra-node"} from the checkout Deployment pod template (patch deployment/checkout in astronomy-shop) so the pending ReplicaSet pods can schedule on sregym-worker/sregym-worker2/sregym-worker3 and the checkout Service regains endpoints; alternatively, if the selector is intended, provision a node labeled kubernetes.io/hostname=extra-node. Verify with kube_deployment_status_replicas_available{deployment="checkout"} and the checkout endpoints object.

gaps: The change_history integration is not configured for this run, so who or what introduced the checkout nodeSelector and when it was changed could not be verified beyond managedFieldsSummary showing an 'Update' by kubectl-client-side-apply at 2026-11-24T03:31:36Z and by OpenAPI-Generator at 03:31:42Z (which fields each write changed is not recorded).

Prometheus range queries returned no_data for every expression attempted in this run (e.g. sum(traces_span_metrics_calls_total) over 03:28-03:31:53Z), so no time-series trend or baseline before/after 03:31:36Z could be established; only instant readings at 2026-11-24T03:31:53Z are used.

Jaeger's newest data was ~2026-11-24T03:31:32Z and 63 frontend log lines fall after the 03:31:53Z window end, so request failures after the 03:31:36Z rollout were not directly observed; the ongoing outage is asserted from 0 ready/available replicas and the endpoint-less checkout Service at 03:31:53Z.

The pre-rollout checkout ReplicaSet checkout-6c769b88b5 and its pod checkout-6c769b88b5-ntls4 no longer exist, so whether that template already contained the nodeSelector (i.e. a prior edit before 03:31:36Z) is unknown, as are that pod's logs.

Kubernetes objects are point-in-time readings taken at 03:31:55-03:32:17Z; event history before 2026-11-24T02:38:49Z is not retained, so earlier checkout availability in the one-day incident window is unknown.
Whether frontend-proxy and load-generator error spans share the same root cause is not proven from their own span details; only their STATUS_CODE_ERROR counts were observed.
next_steps: Disable or remove the kubernetes.io/hostname=extra-node nodeSelector on Deployment checkout in namespace astronomy-shop and confirm the ReplicaSet pods schedule.
After the patch, confirm checkout endpoints are repopulated and that frontend POST /api/checkout returns http.status_code 200 with no STATUS_CODE_ERROR spans.

Audit who holds the kubectl-client-side-apply / OpenAPI-Generator writers on deployment/checkout to prevent re-application of the bad nodeSelector (Kubernetes audit log or change history would be needed).
Add an alert on kube_deployment_status_replicas_available{deployment=~"checkout|payment|cart"} == 0 and on kube_pod_status_unschedulable == 1 to catch scheduling-driven outages sooner.
